statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains below the blocking threshold while macro Stress is extreme.
recommendation: The current public state remains green; the principal conditional risk window is the PPI/claims-to-cash-open sequence from 12:15 to 14:30 UTC.
headline: Low Tail, extreme Stress ahead of U.S. inflation data
body: Fresh macro evidence remains hostile: Brent is above $100 and the U.S. 10-year yield is near 4.84%. The freshest independently verified delayed NQ evidence is mixed rather than persistently one-way, so Tail remains low despite extreme Stress. PPI and claims at 12:30 UTC are the next major price-discovery checkpoint.

sources.title: Asian stocks wilt as Brent holds above $100, yields near 2023 peak
Dow Jones Futures Rise After Oil Prices, Yields Hit Stocks; Inflation Data Due

lookbackSummary: Published ChatGPT history shows Tail rising from WATCH to a 43% high during the September 9 downside episode, then decaying through the U.S. afternoon and overnight as the path became more mixed. One 12:00 UTC historical slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours remain dominated by extreme macro Stress from energy, yields and inflation-event risk. Forecast Tail stays below the block threshold unless post-PPI or cash-open trading develops persistent extension, shallow pullbacks or failed retracements; CPI on September 11 remains a later checkpoint outside this 24-hour window.

forecast.analysis: At the cutoff, the freshest independently verified delayed NQ quote remained near 29,472, while later reporting described Nasdaq futures only modestly lower. Oil above $100 and a 10-year yield near 4.84% keep stress extreme, but no verified persistent one-way NQ path is established.
drivers: Delayed NQ evidence does not verify persistent extension
10-year Treasury yield remains near multi-year highs

news.title: Asian stocks wilt as Brent holds above $100, yields near 2023 peak
Brent holds above $100 as tanker attacks deepen supply fear

forecast.analysis: Absent a fresh directional break, the early-European transition is expected to remain mixed. Tail stays low unless NQ begins holding near an overnight extreme with shallow pullbacks while yields and oil continue to reinforce the same direction.
drivers: Persistent NQ extension would be the key Tail trigger

news.title: Asian stocks wilt as Brent holds above $100, yields near 2023 peak

forecast.analysis: European cash trading may add cross-asset information, but the forecast remains non-directional. A move in NQ would need repeated extension or failed retracements, not merely weak European equities, to justify a higher Tail state.
drivers: Failed NQ retracements would raise Tail

forecast.analysis: With U.S. inflation data still several hours away, event anticipation mainly supports extreme Stress rather than Tail. The low-Tail base case persists if NQ continues to show meaningful two-way trade rather than efficient directional extension.
drivers: Two-way NQ trade would limit Tail

forecast.analysis: Pre-U.S. positioning may increase volatility without implying mean-reversion failure. Tail remains low unless the price path begins compressing pullbacks and repeatedly extending toward a session extreme.
drivers: Pullback depth is the primary path checkpoint
Brent above $100 remains a macro stressor

forecast.analysis: As U.S. participation builds, a broader range is plausible, but event proximity alone does not lift Tail above the blocking threshold. The main check is whether NQ remains two-sided or starts producing repeated failed retracements.
drivers: Event proximity raises Stress more than Tail
Repeated failed retracements would change the regime

forecast.analysis: Within roughly ninety minutes of PPI, headline and positioning sensitivity rises. The mapped forecast moves to WATCH, but any higher Tail state would require actual post-release persistence rather than the scheduled release itself.
drivers: Initial jobless claims share the 12:30 UTC window
Post-release persistence is not yet observed

forecast.analysis: This hour contains the 12:30 UTC PPI and claims releases. Stress reaches the ceiling and Tail is WATCH-level; escalation beyond 24% is conditional on an observed one-way repricing with shallow pullbacks, repeated extension, or aligned yields and breadth.
drivers: Post-release NQ pullback quality is the decisive checkpoint

forecast.analysis: The first full post-PPI hour overlaps the approach to the U.S. cash open. Tail remains capped at WATCH in the forecast unless the released data is followed by persistent NQ extension and weak retracement depth across the opening transition.
drivers: Persistent extension would be required for a block state

forecast.analysis: The cash-open hour also contains Existing-Home Sales at 14:00 UTC. Whipsaw risk stays high, while Tail remains below the block threshold unless the opening auction produces one-way continuation and repeated failed pullbacks.
drivers: Opening-auction continuation is the key Tail checkpoint

forecast.analysis: By this hour, orderly retracement after the data/open would support a lower Tail reading, while continued extension without meaningful pullbacks would keep the WATCH state elevated. Stress remains extreme because oil and rates are still restrictive backdrops.
drivers: Continuation without pullbacks would prevent Tail decay

forecast.analysis: If the opening move has developed two-way trade by mid-session, Tail should ease toward the lower WATCH band. A renewed second leg would matter more than the original data surprise, especially if yields and NQ direction re-align.

The forecast assumes no persistent second leg unless evidence emerges. Tail stays at WATCH because late-morning continuation can still develop, but the score would fall quickly if NQ retraces materially and cross-assets stabilize.
drivers: Meaningful NQ retracement would reduce Tail

forecast.analysis: In the early afternoon, Tail returns to low under a two-way price-path assumption. A fresh extreme-holding move with failed pullbacks would invalidate that assumption and require a higher state in the next assessment.
drivers: Two-way trade is the base assumption
Extreme holding would invalidate the low-Tail case

forecast.analysis: Without a renewed directional catalyst, the afternoon base case is mixed rather than trending. Stress remains high from energy and rates, but those factors alone do not establish the pathological price path measured by Tail.
drivers: Energy and rates remain macro stressors

forecast.analysis: Approaching the final two hours of cash trading, the forecast keeps Tail low unless NQ begins a late-session one-way extension. A balanced tape would keep the stress signal separate from Tail.
drivers: Balanced trade would keep Tail low

forecast.analysis: The cash-session close can amplify directional flow, but no future continuation is assumed. Tail remains low unless closing activity produces persistent extension with little retracement and aligned index components.
drivers: Persistent late extension would be the risk trigger

forecast.analysis: After the cash close, thinner liquidity can exaggerate moves. The forecast remains low-Tail because no one-way structure is presumed; any abrupt extension would need confirmation from subsequent retracement behavior.

Evening trade is expected to be quieter, with Tail low unless geopolitical headlines create a fresh discontinuity. The known oil-supply backdrop keeps Stress elevated but does not by itself imply NQ mean-reversion failure.
drivers: Oil-supply disruption remains a persistent stressor

forecast.analysis: As the next Asia session begins, the focus shifts to whether overnight markets absorb the prior U.S. move. Tail remains low unless NQ holds an overnight extreme while Asian equities, yields, and oil align in the same direction.
drivers: Overnight extreme holding would raise Tail
Cross-asset alignment is required for escalation

forecast.analysis: Overnight risk begins to incorporate the next U.S. CPI checkpoint later on September 11. That calendar risk mainly lifts Stress; Tail remains low unless the overnight price path becomes persistently directional before the release.
drivers: Next-day CPI remains a future checkpoint
Overnight directional efficiency would raise Tail
Calendar risk mainly affects Stress before release

forecast.analysis: Asian-session price discovery may broaden the range ahead of CPI, but the forecast does not assume a trend. Low Tail persists if pullbacks remain meaningful and NQ does not hold at an extreme.
Pre-European overnight trade remains sensitive to energy and rates. Tail is low in the absence of verified one-way structure, while Stress rises modestly as the next inflation release draws closer.

The final forecast hour remains low-Tail under an orderly overnight assumption. A sustained break with shallow retracements before Europe opens would be the main condition requiring a higher Tail state in the subsequent run.
drivers: Orderly overnight trade is the base case
Shallow retracements would invalidate the base case

forecastDetail.comment: Current evidence is mixed: delayed NQ data do not verify one-way extension, while oil and Treasury yields keep Stress extreme.
Early-Europe conditions remain low-Tail unless NQ starts holding an extreme with shallow pullbacks and aligned macro pressure.
European cash trading can add direction, but repeated NQ extension or failed retracements would be required for a higher Tail state.
Pre-event anticipation mainly keeps Stress extreme; low Tail persists under meaningful two-way NQ trade.
Pre-U.S. positioning may widen the range, but Tail stays low unless pullbacks compress and extension becomes persistent.
U.S. participation increases, yet event proximity alone does not lift Tail; repeated failed retracements remain the key checkpoint.
